previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of mechanical aortic valve replacement, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, coronary artery disease, and prior right below-knee amputation was admitted for a poorly healing amputation stump with eschar. She underwent surgical debridement of the stump and VAC placement. Her INR was elevated at admission (4.3), so warfarin was held. Postoperatively, warfarin was restarted and a heparin drip was used for bridging. The VAC was changed multiple times, with good granulation tissue noted on exam. She received dialysis during the admission, with associated transient nausea managed with ondansetron. Her INR rose to 5.1 by discharge, prompting instructions to hold warfarin and follow up for INR monitoring. She was discharged home with visiting nurse support for VAC care and close outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ female with h/o CAD s/p CABG, PCI, AS 
s/p AVR x2 (now w/mechanical valve on coumadin), ESRD s/p 2x 
failed transplants now HD ___, PVD s/p right BKA and

the ED and then transferred to Vascular Surgery on HD3 given 
planned amputation.

-___ Course-
# Nausea and vomiting:  
Unclear etiology. Main ddx includes secondary to hypertension 
vs. a viral infectious process vs. a neuro process given subtle 
hyperdensity in mid-medulla. No e/o type I ACS.  Nausea and 
vomiting resolved overnight and blood pressure is now under 
better control. Recommended to pt. and her husband that they 
have MRI scan to further evaluate medulla lesion seen on CT 
head. After discussion of risks and benefits of MRI, the pt. and 
husband both agreed to decline MRI.

# HTN emergency
Patient presented with BPs in the 180 - 250 range.  End organ 
effects include nausea, vomiting, and troponin leak. Suspect 
initial hypertension was secondary to not taking 
antihypertensives as well as nausea and vomiting. Pt. reports 
that at home she is often in the 180 range, particularly in the 
evenings. She also reports, however, that about ___ her 
BP falls into the low 100s during HD and she becomes 
symptomatic.  

# Anion gap metabolic acidosis
Suspect secondary to sodium thiosulfate administration during HD 
that started on ___ when the gap was first noted.  Lactate 
normal. No ingestions.  Will send ketones given poor PO intake, 
but feel this is unlikely given recent persistent of AG.

# CAD with elevated troponin  
Trop 0.16 x2 with baseline level of 0.09 - 0.11. Most likely 
demand in setting of extensive nausea and vomiting as well as 
hypertension. Patient has not been taking home aspirin, plavix, 
or warfarin in preparation for surgery. EKG is reassuring with 
no evidence of ischemic changes.  

# ESRD: dialysis ___  
- dialysis email sent  
- renal diet when able to tolerate POs  
- cont home calcium acetate when pt able to tolerate POs 
 
# PVD  
Patient with prior plans for admission on ___ for heparin gtt 
48 hours prior to surgery on ___ for amputation of left toe. 

# AVR s/p mechanical valve placement: Subtherapeutic INR on 
admission. Pt.started on heparin gtt in anticipation of surgery. 


-Vascular Surgery Hospital Course-
The patient was transferred to Vascular Surgery on ___. She 
continued on systemic anticoagulation with heparin gtt as well 
as all anti-hypertensive medications that she was on prior to 
transfer.

On ___, she went for dialysis. She became hypertensive again 
with SBP to the 200s and given IV hydralazine to which she 
responded well. She was pre-opped and consented for the OR. 
Pre-op CXR showed bilateral pleural effusions, moderate on the 
right and small on the left consistent with volume overload in 
the setting of hemodialysis.

On the morning of ___, she had an episode of tachypnea, 
nausea, and hypertension (SBP to 170s-200s). Tachypnea improved 
with supplemental O2, and IV hydralazine decreased SBP to 170s. 
EKG done showed no significant changes from prior. For her 
nausea, she was given a scopolamine patch, Zofran, and Ativan. 

She was taken to the operating room on ___ for amputation. 
The patient underwent a left ___ toe amputation (not the 
previously planned left TMA given that her toe gangrene had 
significantly improved). She tolerated the procedure quite well 
and returned to the floor for post-operative care. 

On ___, she had another hemodialysis session. The wound vac 
at her RLE stump was changed now showing a shallow, clean wound 
with healthy granulation tissue. Cardiology was consulted for 
management of hypertension. Per their recommendations (as well 
as Nephrology), metoprolol was discontinued and the patient was 
switched to labetalol. Coumadin was also resumed. She 
experienced increased pain in her left foot after dialysis for 
which her Dilaudid dose was increased. 

On ___, the patient was doing better. Her nausea was 
significantly improved, and she was tolerating oral intake well. 
Her pain was also under better control. Her blood pressure was 
under much better control as well with systolics 120s-130s on a 
regimen of labetalol, oral hydralazine, and amlodipine. Her 
amputation wound was intact and clean. Her INR had reached 2 and 
heparin gtt was discontinued. The patient was appropriate for 
discharge and eager to go home.

She was discharged home with previously established ___ services 
for wound care and physical therapy. Her antihypertensive 
regimen on discharge was labetalol, amlodipine and hydralazine. 
Cardiology had recommended perhaps using lisinopril instead of 
hydralazine if Nephrology was comfortable with this. Ms. 
___ wanted to leave this decision to her outpatient 
nephrologist, Dr. ___ she is scheduled to see within the 
week. Her Plavix was discontinued, and she was to continue on 
Coumadin (managed by PCP). She was instructed to keep her 
appointments with her healthcare providers. We also made an 
appointment for her to establish care with Dr. ___ of 
___. She will be seen in Vascular Surgery Clinic in about 
3 weeks for suture removal.

hypertension to 200s.  // eval hemorrhage.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images images of the brain were obtained without
contrast. Coronal and sagittal as well as thin bone-algorithm reconstructed
images were obtained.

DOSE:  DLP:  780.44 mGy-cm
CTDI:  54.42 mGy

COMPARISON:  MRI brain.  ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of infarction or edema.  A small area of hyperdensity in
the right aspect of the medulla is noted, which may be artifactual or may
represent a small area of hemorrhage or even a small lesion (series 2, image
5). The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and configuration for age.
No osseous abnormalities seen. Dense calcifications of the distal vertebral
arteries and carotid siphons are noted. A small air-fluid level is seen in the
left sphenoid sinus. The paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear
cavities are otherwise clear. The orbits are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

Ill-defined hyperdensity in the right aspect of the medulla, which may
represent a artifact, small hemorrhage, or vascular lesion. MRI is recommended
for further evaluation.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  The ill-defined hyperdensity in the right aspect of the
medulla, likely is consistent with artifact. If there is clinical concern,
correlation with MRI is advised.
